requirements.summary: Restore the TrailerModal component so clicking 'Watch Trailer' opens a visible modal with YouTube iframe player
acceptanceCriteria: TrailerModal.tsx contains a functional React component (not an empty file)
The modal opens when triggered from MediaCard click events
A YouTube iframe is rendered inside the modal with the correct trailer video ID
The modal dialog is visible on screen (not hidden by z-index or stacking context issues)

file_operations.description: Implement a functional React component using Radix/Shadcn Dialog that accepts mediaType (movie or tv) and mediaId as props, renders a YouTube iframe for the trailer, and manages open/close state. The Dialog content must use z-index values high enough to render above all page content (Hero, Header, FeaturedRow sections). Include proper TypeScript types for props and ensure the component integrates with the existing glassmorphic design theme.

requirements.summary: Implement trailer fetching logic that queries TMDB API for video/trailer data with proper error handling
acceptanceCriteria: A React Query hook fetches trailer data from TMDB /movie/{id}/videos or /tv/{id}/videos endpoints
The hook handles transient failures (rate limiting, timeouts, network errors) and surfaces them as React Query error states
The hook gracefully handles cases where no trailer exists (empty results array)
The hook uses the resilient TMDB fetch layer with timeouts and rate limiting already established in the codebase

file_operations.description: Add a useGetTrailer React Query hook that fetches trailer/video data from TMDB API given a media type (movie or tv) and media ID. The hook should call the TMDB /movie/{id}/videos or /tv/{id}/videos endpoints using the existing resilient fetch layer with timeout and rate limiting. Return the first YouTube trailer from results, handle empty results gracefully, and surface network errors, rate limits, and timeouts as React Query error states. Use proper TypeScript types for the trailer response structure.

requirements.summary: Update MediaCard to trigger TrailerModal when 'Watch Trailer' is clicked
acceptanceCriteria: MediaCard includes a 'Watch Trailer' button or clickable area in the hover overlay
Clicking triggers an onClick handler that opens the TrailerModal with the correct media type and ID
The interaction works consistently across all MediaCard instances (Featured, Netflix Top 10, Trending sections)

file_operations.description: Add a 'Watch Trailer' button to the hover overlay section (alongside the existing title and rating display). Wire the button's onClick handler to open the TrailerModal, passing the media item's type (movie or tv) and ID. Use state management to control the modal's open/close state. Ensure the button styling matches the glassmorphic theme and the interaction works consistently across all usage contexts (FeaturedRow, NetflixTop10).

requirements.summary: Display explicit UI states in TrailerModal for loading, no trailer available, and fetch errors
acceptanceCriteria: While fetching trailer data, the modal shows a loading indicator
If no trailer exists in TMDB results, the modal shows a clear 'No trailer available' message
If the fetch fails (network error, rate limit, timeout), the modal shows an error message with a 'Try Again' button
Clicking 'Try Again' triggers a new fetch attempt via React Query
The modal never shows a blank/empty state when a trailer fetch is in progress or has failed

file_operations.description: Inside the TrailerModal component, consume the useGetTrailer hook and implement three distinct UI states: (1) Loading state with a spinner or skeleton while isLoading is true, (2) No trailer state with a user-friendly 'No trailer available' message when data is null or empty, (3) Error state with an error message and a 'Try Again' button that calls React Query's refetch when the hook returns an error. Ensure the modal never shows a blank state during fetch operations. Style all states consistently with the glassmorphic design theme.

requirements.summary: Configure TrailerModal Dialog with high z-index to ensure visibility above all page content
acceptanceCriteria: The Dialog content and overlay render with z-index values that ensure visibility above Hero, Header, FeaturedRow, and all other page sections
The modal is fully visible and clickable in production builds (not just development)
No stacking context issues cause the modal or its video iframe to be hidden behind other elements

file_operations.description: Apply explicit className overrides or inline styles to the Radix Dialog overlay and content components, setting z-index values high enough to render above all existing page elements (Header, Hero, FeaturedRow sections). Verify the z-index values work in production builds and that no stacking context issues cause the modal or iframe to be hidden. Test across all page contexts where MediaCard instances appear.

requirements.summary: Manage TrailerModal state transitions to ensure reliable re-fetching and rendering when reopened
acceptanceCriteria: Closing and reopening the modal triggers a fresh trailer fetch (or uses valid cached data)
Switching between different media items (e.g., clicking Watch Trailer on multiple cards) correctly updates the modal's content without stale iframe state
The YouTube iframe key or src is updated appropriately to force re-render when the trailer ID changes
The modal's internal state (loading, error, iframe rendering) transitions cleanly across open/close cycles

file_operations.description: Ensure the TrailerModal's internal state and useGetTrailer hook properly reset when the modal is closed and reopened. Use React Query's enabled option or key-based invalidation to trigger fresh fetches when mediaId or mediaType changes. Set a unique key prop on the YouTube iframe element based on the trailer ID to force re-render when the trailer changes. Handle the transition between loading, error, and success states cleanly across multiple open/close cycles, ensuring no stale iframe src or state persists.

Ensure the MediaCard's state management for opening/closing the TrailerModal properly passes updated mediaType and mediaId on each click. When a user clicks 'Watch Trailer' on a different MediaCard, the modal should receive the new media information and trigger a fresh fetch or use valid cached data from React Query. Verify that switching between different media items works correctly without stale state.
